functional_semantics.triton: per row: mean, biased var, rstd = rsqrt(var+eps), y = (x-mean)*rstd*w + b, fp32 stats, output in x dtype (impl_triton.py:22-44).
functional_semantics.note: Both match impl_torch.py:6 (F.layer_norm over the last dim, eps default 1e-5). Generator tensors.py:403-407 returns (x, weight, bias); eps not supplied by config, so both use the signature default.

stages.triton: contiguous().reshape view (impl_triton.py:71), empty_like (72-73), one launch grid (batch_M,) (75-92).
stages.cutile: views + weight/bias contiguous no-ops (impl_cutile.py:82-86), one launch grid (batch_M,1,1) (89,108-110).
stages.note: Stats and apply fused in one kernel, one program per row, on both sides.

dependencies.triton: apply pass depends on mean/rstd of the same row (impl_triton.py:31-34,43).

reduction_scan_sort.triton: lane-wise sum and sum-of-squares over chunks, one tl.sum each, var = E[x^2] - mean^2 (impl_triton.py:22-33).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Both use the one-pass variance; the contract permits any fp32 formulation (one-pass, centred, Welford) since verification is tolerance-based.

precision.triton: fp32 upcast of x, weight, bias; fp32 stats; fp32 result stored to the output pointer with implicit cast (impl_triton.py:27,40-44).
precision.cutile: fp32 upcast of x, weight, bias; explicit ct.astype to x.dtype at store (impl_cutile.py:30-35,51-63).
precision.note: Same precision path; implicit vs explicit final cast is a primitive detail.

preprocessing.triton: x.contiguous().reshape (view) + empty_like inside run; weight/bias passed as-is (impl_triton.py:71-73,79).
preprocessing.note: Nothing cached or prepacked; both run() signatures lack **kwargs (engine passes only autotune).

hardware_dispatch.triton: no dispatch branches; masked loads with other=0.0/1.0/0.0 for x/weight/bias (impl_triton.py:27,41-42).
hardware_dispatch.cutile: no dispatch branches; zero-padded loads for all three (impl_cutile.py:33,54,60); fixed allow_tma=False/latency=1 hints.
hardware_dispatch.note: Tail fill values differ (weight other=1.0 vs zero pad) but masked lanes are never stored; mapping detail.

fq_boundary.note: n = batch*M*K (tensors.py:699-700). Counts X read twice (statistics + apply passes) plus Y written once, matching both kernels' row re-read; the (K,) weight/bias reads are uncounted. This two-pass convention differs from l2_norm's compulsory 2n model: an on-chip single-read design would be credited with 3n bytes. Nothing is untimed or prepacked; views and allocation are inside run().
